brief.ask: Art-direct "Alabaster & Gold Kintsugi" — #12 of the 72 Ambo church visualizers (Calm Contemporary Worship lyric visualizer, Collection I of 72; subgenre Contemporary Abstract). Premise: Dark charcoal-alabaster stone slabs repaired with molten 24k gold-leaf veins. Inspired by Japanese Kintsugi ("golden repair") and brokenness made whole: tectonic dark stone slabs glow with branching molten gold seams and lacquer nodes. Lighting today: Key: Grazing side light across matte stone + emissive 3500K gold veins. Service use: Grace, redemption, healing, confession & assurance of pardon. Audio mapping today: Vocal → Pulses liquid 24k gold luminescence along the Kintsugi fracture network; Swell → Spreads warm golden halation out from the branching stone seams; Harmonic → Illuminates golden lacquer repair nodes. Palette: #0E0E12 #232229 #D4AF37 #FFF5D6. Keep the id, name, premise and palette; rebuild the direction: the geometry and depth planes, typography for the worship lyric band (one line at a time, four to five seconds a line, word-by-word progression), image logic (how the Gemini concept plate it twins (/sanctuary-plates/scripture-kintsugi-mineral-gold.jpg, blended in at plateBlend) and the procedural scene meet), texture, motion, and which audio channel drives what. Decide it — the lead's lens will drive the kit's material weave and optical pass for this one.
brief.audience: Congregations watching a projector or LED wall from the pews, five to forty metres away, eyes on the words; and the worship leader or volunteer running Ambo live from a laptop.
brief.feeling: Stillness and reverence — a sanctuary that breathes with the singer's voice; gorgeous, slow, never a screensaver.
constraints: Build method (fixed): a real-time Canvas 2D audio-reactive renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit — sanctuary background, multi-plane depth (god rays, motes, bokeh), the kit's Council optical pass (35mm light leaks, anamorphic flare, film grain, colour punch, and a tactile material weave keyed to the LEAD director's lens) and the kit's lyric / scripture typography engine. No video playback, no WebGL, no assets beyond the one concept plate.

Audio drives amplitude, colour, light, growth and glow only — never the position of the words. Envelopes are smoothed; nothing strobes or flashes (photosensitive-safe); uptempo pulses are spring-damped.

The reading band is sacred: lyrics or scripture must stay legible at 1920×1080 and 4K from the back pew, over the busiest moment of the scene. A text-safe dimming band is part of the kit; direct how the scene yields to it.

Typefaces are fixed to the kit's open-licensed set: Noto Serif (text serif), Outfit / Inter (sans), Cinzel (display), JetBrains Mono. Direct scale, case, tracking, measure and hierarchy, not new families.

Sacred imagery is used correctly and respectfully: biblical places and objects are specific and attributable, never costume; nothing denominational or branded; nothing that reads as a music video or a screensaver.
Runs at 60 fps on an integrated-GPU laptop driving a projector: favour layered gradients, cached textures and a few large shapes over particle storms.
Keep this visualizer's id, name, premise and four-colour palette. The council owns the direction, not the catalogue entry.
references: Concept plate: /sanctuary-plates/scripture-kintsugi-mineral-gold.jpg — a Gemini art plate this visualizer was built as the interactive code twin of.
Sample lyric lines on the band: "Be still my soul the Lord is on thy side" / "Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain".

proposals.title: The Measure That Holds
proposals.idea: A φ-governed cantus firmus — declared as code constant before the render loop opens — makes every gold seam, every lacquer node, every luminance beat a trigonometric consequence of one structural law, so the congregation reads stillness even when the scene breathes.
proposals.geometry: A horizontal golden-section cut divides the canvas at φ⁻¹ ≈ 0.618 from the top: the lyric band occupies the lower 0.382 zone; the tectonic stone field owns the upper 0.618. Within the stone field, three vertical slab edges are placed at φ-derived intervals (canvas_width × [0.236, 0.382, 0.618]) — not decorative, not gestural, structurally prior. The Kintsugi fracture network is a Lindenmayer branching system whose trunk angle and branch ratios are trigonometric functions of φ, exported as a named constant CANTUS_PHI before any draw call. Every gold seam terminus, every lacquer node, every god-ray vanishing point is derived from that constant. Depth is three planes: (1) rearmost — the concept plate blended at plateBlend, which is the luminance authority; (2) mid — procedural stone slabs with matte normal-map simulation; (3) foreground — emissive gold fracture overlay and sparse bokeh mote
proposals.typography: Cinzel, tracked at +0.12em, set in Small Caps for the lyric line — not for decoration but because Cinzel's Roman proportion gives each glyph a column width that holds at 40 metres. Body size: 5.2vw at 1080p, scaling by viewport√ to 4K. The active line is set at full luminance (#FFF5D6, the palette's warm cream); the preceding ghost line, fading out over 400ms, drops to 28% opacity of the same cream — never a second colour, never a typeface switch. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 120ms with a spring-damped opacity curve (stiffness 180, damping 22); no lateral movement, no scale pulse — the word arrives, it holds, it is read. Line transitions: the completed line rests for 600ms, then dissolves over 400ms as the new line enters from 0% opacity. Measure: no lyric line exceeds 32 characters; if the source line is longer, the engine breaks at a syntactic boundary. Tracking widens
proposals.imageLogic: The concept plate /sanctuary-plates/scripture-kintsugi-mineral-gold.jpg is the luminance authority — it governs, it does not accompany. At boot, the plate is sampled into a 24×14 grid of linear-light luminance values; these values are frozen as a structural constant (PLATE_LUMA_GRID) and used for three purposes only: (1) seeding bokeh mote positions — a mote is permitted only where PLATE_LUMA_GRID exceeds 0.55; (2) weighting god-ray origin points — rays emerge from the two highest-luminance columns in the grid; (3) setting the ambient fill level of the stone slabs — darker grid cells produce cooler (#232229) slab fill, brighter cells warm toward #D4AF37. The plate itself is composited as the rearmost plane at plateBlend (operator: luminosity blend, clamped 0.18–0.52), so it reads as inherited light rather than a photograph. proposals.texture: Stone surface: a tileable normal-map simulation rendered as a cached offscreen canvas at 512×512 — Perlin noise at two octaves (scale 0.004, 0.018), output remapped to a surface-normal field and used to modulate the grazing side-light (key light at 14° elevation, 8° azimuth from left). The matte stone reads as alabaster-charcoal, never glossy. Gold veins: emissive, not reflective — they are drawn as Bézier strokes at 2.4px base width, with a radial glow (blur radius 18px, #D4AF37 at 60% opacity) composited above the stone layer. proposals.motion: Temporal hierarchy obeys the same law as spatial hierarchy — the measure is stated before the content exists. Entry sequence: (1) 0.0s — plate fades in at plateBlend over 0.6s; (2) 0.6s — stone slab edges draw in from left at 120ms depth-order intervals, each slab arriving before the next; (3) 1.2s — gold fracture network grows along the L-system path at 1.4s completion, trunk first, branches in generation order, never all at once; (4) 2.6s — lyric band fades in; (5) 3.0s — first word appears. Audio mapping — Vocal amplitude (smoothed, 12-frame envelope): pulses the emissive luminance of the fracture network between base 60% and peak 92%, spring-damped (stiffness 120, damping 18); also widens Cinzel tracking by +0.008em per unit. proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60fps target on integrated GPU. All geometry is procedural: L-system fractures computed once at load and cached as a Path2D object; stone normals baked to an offscreen canvas at init; bokeh motes stored as a typed Float32Array of (x, y, r, luma) structs seeded at load. Per-frame draw order: (1) clear with #0E0E12; (2) blit plate at plateBlend (luminosity composite); (3) blit stone normal layer with side-light modulation; (4) draw fracture Path2D with emissive glow (shadowBlur, shadowColor); (5) draw lacquer nodes; (6) draw bokeh motes (globalAlpha keyed to PLATE_LUMA_GRID); (7) draw god rays as radial gradient wedges; (8) composite Council optical pass (grain, flare, vignette, linen weave — all pre-cached canvases); (9) draw text-safe band; (10) render lyric. proposals.humanTrace: The grazing side-light angle (14°, 8° azimuth) was chosen by directing the shader as a cinematographer directs a practical — it is the angle at which real alabaster slab edges catch and hold without specular blow-out. The L-system branching ratios were tuned by ear against the sample lyric 'Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain' — the fracture network had to feel like a held breath, not a map. The linen-tooth overlay is the sign of the page: this stone has been written on. The word-by-word spring curve was timed against a spoken reading of the lyric at contemplative pace — 120ms per word is the interval at which the congregation can receive, not merely see.
proposals.risk: The φ-grid is legible to those who feel structure subconsciously; it risks reading as cold or over-engineered to a congregation expecting warmth. The counter: the gold seams are the warmth, and the grid is what makes them feel inevitable rather than decorative. The greater risk is that the Baroque Dramatist will argue the fracture network should announce itself — bloom on the downbeat, scale on the chorus. I will not concede that point. A reveal that announces itself is a reveal that has already spent its authority. The fracture network must already be complete when the congregation enters, holding its light quietly, so that the vocal pulse feels like recognition, not spectacle.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the fracture network to grow during the service — a living reveal, branching on the chorus, scaling on the swell. I argue that growth on the downbeat is a theatrical gesture that subordinates the lyric to the scene: the congregation looks at the stone, not the word. proposals.title: Fracture First, Then Gold
proposals.idea: The stone breaks visibly before it heals — the repair is earned, not cosmetic, because the fracture network is a prior physical commitment the entire luminance pass must answer to.
proposals.geometry: A single tectonic slab occupies the full canvas. Before any glow is drawn, a procedural fracture graph is generated at init: eight to twelve primary crack vectors radiate from two declared fault-origin points (placed at roughly 38% x / 55% y and 61% x / 42% y — eccentric, not centred, not golden-ratio-tidy) and branch into tertiary hairlines at angles sampled from a seeded noise field. These vectors are cached as a polyline network — the registration plate the entire render is accountable to. Depth is three planes: background slab (static, deep), a mid-plane of displaced slab fragments drifting at sub-pixel scale (0.3–0.8 px over 8–14 s, spring-damped), and a foreground lacquer-node layer of 14–18 discrete repair blobs. No radial symmetry. No grid. The fractures decide everything else.
proposals.typography: Cinzel Regular, sentence-case — Cinzel carries lapidary weight without requiring a paid foundry; it reads like stone-cut inscription. Single lyric line centred horizontally, seated 68% down the canvas (below the primary fault origin, in quieter stone territory). Cap-height: 7.2% of canvas height at 1080p, scaling linearly to 4K. Letter-spacing: 0.18em — wide enough to breathe across a 40-metre throw but not so wide it atomises the phrase. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 18 frames (300 ms) with a simultaneous 0.4 px upward drift from rest, then settles. No blur, no bounce — the word arrives like weight being set down. The text-safe band is a gradient from #0E0E12 at full opacity (bottom 18% of canvas) rising to 0% opacity at 26%; the lyric sits inside that band. Scripture reference (if present) in Noto Serif Italic, 38% of lyric scale, 1.5 line-heights below, tracking 0.08em.
proposals.imageLogic: The concept plate /sanctuary-plates/scripture-kintsugi-mineral-gold.jpg enters as a texture authority, not a backdrop. It is blended via plateBlend in multiply mode at 0.32 opacity over the procedural slab layer — its mineral detail (existing crack stains, alabaster veining, lacquer texture) modulates the procedural surface without overriding it. The plate is never scaled to fill; it tiles at 1.4× canvas, offset by a slow drift (0.04 px/s horizontal, 0.02 px/s vertical) so the texture reads as continuous stone, not a photograph. Wherever the procedural fracture polylines run, the plate's luminance at that pixel is sampled and fed back into the gold-vein emissive calculation — the photograph earns its presence by informing the physics of the glow, not decorating the surface.
proposals.texture: Slab surface: a 512×512 cached noise texture (Perlin, two octaves, #0E0E12 to #232229) baked at init, never redrawn — this is the stone tooth. Over it, the fracture polylines are rendered at 1.5–3 px stroke width with a feathered outer glow (radial gradient, #D4AF37 at 0 radius to transparent at 18 px) — the gold seam has physical weight, not a neon edge. Lacquer nodes are filled ellipses (semi-axes 6–14 px, each unique, not cloned) with a specular highlight offset 35° from a declared key-light azimuth — same angle across every node, because a single light source is a physical fact. Film grain: a 256×256 luminance noise canvas composited at 0.08 opacity, re-seeded every 3 frames (not every frame — 20 fps grain refresh is enough tooth without cost). The council optical pass adds the 35mm light-leak strip (one edge, warm amber, soft, stationary — not animated) and one anamorphic flare stre
proposals.motion: Init (0–2 s): slab emerges from black via a luminance ramp on the noise texture — stone becomes visible before gold. Fracture draw (2–4 s): polylines trace themselves from fault origins outward at a declared draw speed (canvas units per frame), not all at once — the break happens in real time, once, at start, never repeated. Lacquer nodes bloom in after their branch reaches them. Then the scene breathes. Vocal amplitude → pulses liquid luminance along the fracture polylines: a travelling brightness envelope moves from fault origin outward, speed proportional to amplitude, spring-damped so it never strobes. Swell → the outer halation radius of every gold seam expands (max +12 px at full swell), easing out over 1.4 s, easing back over 2.8 s. Harmonic → lacquer node specular intensity lifts: the 35° highlight brightens, not the fill — the repair points catch more light without changing colo
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer. Init phase: generate fracture graph (seeded RNG, cached as Float32 polyline arrays); bake slab noise texture to offscreen canvas; sample concept plate into a second offscreen canvas for luminance-lookup. Per-frame: clear → draw slab noise (blitfrom cache) → multiply plate overlay → draw fracture polylines with audio-driven glow width → draw lacquer nodes with audio-driven specular → draw mid-plane fragment offsets → apply text-safe gradient band → render lyric band → composite grain canvas → composite optical pass (light-leak strip, anamorphic streak, colour punch LUT as a per-channel curve on a sample of canvas pixels). All animated values run through a single shared envelope smoother (exponential moving average, α = 0.12 for fast channels, 0.04 for swell) before touching draw calls. Target: under 4 ms per frame on integrated GPU.
proposals.humanTrace: The fracture graph's two fault-origin points are declared constants chosen by a human editor before the first frame renders — they are eccentric, specific, and not derivable from any grid or ratio. Every downstream light calculation (glow centre, specular offset, flare position, plate-sample lookup) answers to those two coordinates. That prior human decision functions like a registration mark on a press: the whole run is accountable to it. The 35° key-light azimuth is a second declared constant, also chosen before code runs. The lacquer nodes are individually parameterised (not instanced clones) — their semi-axes, rotation, and specular intensity are set values, not procedurally varied at runtime. The imperfection is authored, not generated.
proposals.risk: The fracture draws itself once at start and never again. If a congregation arrives mid-service, they see a healed stone, not the break — they miss the repair being earned. That is the risk. It is worth it because kintsugi is not a loop; the mending happened. Showing the break only once, at the beginning of the service, treats the theology correctly. A screensaver loops. This doesn't.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the fracture to re-draw on every chorus climax — the break blooming and healing in real time as a recurring emotional event. I reject this. Re-drawing the fracture on demand turns a wound into a visual effect. The stone broke once. The gold is permanent. proposals.title: Fracture Network as State Machine
proposals.idea: The Kintsugi repair network is declared once as a procedural graph of vertices and weighted edges — a fixed generative contract — so that every audio event (vocal pulse, swell, harmonic node) is a state change propagating through that graph, not a decorative glow placed on top of it.
proposals.geometry: A Voronoi-seeded fracture graph, seed points drawn from a 7×4 jittered grid (28 nodes) on the 16:9 canvas, edges computed once at init and cached as a polyline atlas. Fracture lines are not random: each edge weight encodes a 'repair priority' scalar (0.0–1.0) that controls gold luminance ceiling. Two dominant tectonic planes split the canvas at approximately 38° and 127°, creating a shallow X-fault that the lyric band bisects horizontally at the lower-third. Stone slab faces occupy the negative space between edges — five to seven large closed polygons, never small shards. Depth is declared as three planes: rear slab (darkest, slowest parallax), mid fracture network (gold veins live here), fore bokeh + mote plane (lightest, fastest response). No radial symmetry; no φ-grid; the rule is tectonic stress, not classical proportion.
proposals.typography: Noto Serif, set in sentence case — not all-caps, not title case — at 4.2vw on 1080p (scales linearly). Tracking: +0.04em. Line measure: max 22 characters (one lyric line fits without wrap). The lyric band sits at 68% vertical, left-edge-anchored at 8% canvas width — offset from centre to rhyme with the dominant 38° fault running upper-left to lower-right. Word-by-word progression: each incoming word fades in over 180ms, previous words dim to 55% opacity but stay visible (the full line remains readable; only luminance hierarchy shifts). Active word: #FFF5D6 at full opacity. Settled words: #FFF5D6 at 55%. Outgoing line: cross-fades to 0% over 400ms as next line enters. Scripture reference, if shown, uses JetBrains Mono at 1.4vw, tracking +0.12em, #D4AF37 at 60% opacity — below the lyric band, right-aligned, so it reads as annotation not headline. No Cinzel; Cinzel's imperial register is wr
proposals.imageLogic: The concept plate /sanctuary-plates/scripture-kintsugi-mineral-gold.jpg is loaded once and drawn as the bottommost canvas layer at full bleed, blended with globalAlpha = plateBlend (kit-controlled, nominal 0.28). A luminance sample pass — 32×18 readings from the plate — is computed at init and stored as a float32 array. This array is the sole authority for where bokeh motes may appear: a mote is only spawned at a canvas coordinate whose plate luminance sample exceeds 0.55, meaning the plate's own tonal geography licences every mote position. The plate is not decorative wallpaper; it is a coordinate permission system. On top of the plate, the procedural fracture graph is drawn with canvas lineTo paths — the plate's mineral texture bleeds through the vector lines because the stone polygon fills are drawn at globalAlpha 0.82 over it, not at 1.0. The gold veins are drawn last in this stack,
proposals.texture: Stone slab faces: filled with a two-stop radial gradient from #232229 (centre) to #0E0E12 (edge), with a per-frame film grain pass (8×8 noise tile, pre-generated as an offscreen canvas at init, drawn at globalAlpha 0.06 + 0.02 × vocalAmp) — grain responds to the vocal channel so the stone itself seems to breathe without moving. Gold veins: stroked at 2.5px base width, shadowBlur = 18 + 24 × vocalAmp, shadowColor = #D4AF37. A secondary stroke at 1px, #FFF5D6, globalAlpha = 0.4 × vocalAmp, runs the same path to simulate the hot core of a liquid seam. Lacquer nodes: filled circles at fracture intersections, radius = 6 + 4 × harmonicAmp, with a two-stop radial gradient from #FFF5D6 (centre) to #D4AF37 (edge) — they read as pooled gold, not sparkle. No particle emitters; no per-particle physics; the 28 node positions are fixed and the luminance is driven, not the geometry.
proposals.motion: Init (0–600ms): stone slabs fade in from #0E0E12 at 0% to full fill over 600ms — no fly-in, no wipe, just a slow material reveal as if light is finding the stone. Fracture lines draw on at init using a recursive graph traversal from the two dominant fault intersections outward, each segment animating its strokeDashoffset from full to zero over 80ms per segment, total draw time 900ms — this is the only 'reveal' and it happens once. Steady state: the scene does not animate unless audio drives it. Vocal amplitude → gold vein shadowBlur and the hot-core stroke opacity, spring-damped (stiffness 0.12, damping 0.72) so pulses arrive as swells not flashes. Swell amplitude → a warm halation: a radial gradient centred on the primary fault intersection, from #D4AF37 at 0% opacity (base) to max 18% opacity at peak swell, radius scaling from 15% to 35% of canvas width — it spreads, it does not flash.
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D only. At init: (1) load and draw plate to offscreen canvas, sample luminance grid, store as Float32Array; (2) generate 28 Voronoi seed points from jittered 7×4 grid, compute Delaunay edges, filter to fracture topology by retaining only edges whose midpoint falls within 12% of one of the two tectonic fault lines — this is the repair priority scalar assignment pass; (3) pre-render film grain tile (256×256 offscreen canvas, one-time noise fill); (4) pre-render bokeh mote positions from luminance-licensed coordinates. Per frame: clear → draw plate (globalAlpha plateBlend) → draw stone polygon fills → draw film grain tile tiled across canvas → draw fracture polylines with audio-driven glow → draw lacquer nodes → draw halation radial gradient → draw lyric band dim rect → draw lyric text. All draw calls use cached path objects; no recomputation of fracture geometry per frame. Target:
proposals.humanTrace: The fracture graph's seed jitter is not random per session — it is seeded from a fixed integer (12, the visualizer's catalogue index) so the topology is repeatable and editable by the team. The 'repair priority' scalars on each edge were set by editorial judgment: the two edges crossing the lyric band's vertical zone were assigned priority 0.3 (dimmer, quieter) so the text zone is structurally calmer than the upper slab. That is a directed compositional decision encoded as a data constant, not an aesthetic accident.
proposals.risk: The risk is that a fully graph-declared, audio-as-state-change system reads as cold or clinical in a context that asks for warmth and reverence. The counter-argument is that the warmth comes from the material simulation (grain, shadowBlur, 3500K gold colour), not from gestural looseness — and that a system which holds still when the audio holds still is the correct reverence model. A screensaver moves whether you speak or not. This does not.

I have already encoded the draw-on traversal as a one-time init event, not a recurring performance. proposals.title: One Fracture, One Light
proposals.idea: A single dominant kintsugi seam — not a network, one load-bearing crack — crosses the full frame as the architecture of the piece, and every audio response is a property of that line, not an addition to it.
proposals.geometry: The frame is divided by one primary fracture running from lower-left to upper-right at approximately 23° off horizontal — a proportion derived from the golden ratio applied to the 1920×1080 field (the break passes through the φ-intersection of width and height). The seam is not centered; it is off-axis enough to create two unequal stone planes, the larger occupying the lower-left two-thirds. Secondary micro-fissures branch from the primary at angles between 12° and 34°, each no longer than 18% of frame width, their endpoint positions fixed as constants in the render loop before any audio state is read — they do not grow at runtime, they are the geology. The text-safe dimming band occupies the lower horizontal third, its upper edge riding just below the primary seam so the fracture reads above the lyric zone at all times. Negative space is the upper-right quadrant: dark stone, almost noth
proposals.typography: Cinzel, caps, tracked at +120 (EM units), weight Regular — not Bold, never Bold; the gold vein is the emphasis, not the letterform. Single lyric line, centered on the text-safe band, set at 5.2vw at 1080p (scales linearly to 4K). Word-by-word reveal: each incoming word fades from 0 to 100% opacity over 18 frames (0.3 s at 60 fps), prior words hold at 72% opacity — present word is the brightest object in the text band, always. Line transition: outgoing line drops to 0% over 24 frames, incoming line begins at frame 12 of that fade (cross-dissolve overlap of 12 frames, 0.2 s). No slide, no lift, no kinetic movement — opacity only. Baseline sits at 82% of frame height. Letter-spacing never changes with audio; only luminance of the text band dimming scrim responds. The scrim is #0E0E12 at 68% opacity, full width, height = 22% of frame — it does not pulse, it does not breathe, it is a fixed ar
proposals.imageLogic: The concept plate /sanctuary-plates/scripture-kintsugi-mineral-gold.jpg is loaded once at init, drawn to an offscreen canvas, and sampled at 32×18 — a luminance map only, no colour. Those 576 luminance readings become the authorization mask for where procedural light may land on the stone planes: high-luminance sample regions permit bokeh motes and god-ray termination points; low-luminance regions are protected darkness. plateBlend is applied as a multiply composite at 0.22 opacity over the procedural stone base — the plate's mineral texture reads as material memory, not as a photograph. The plate never appears at full opacity; it is evidence, not subject. At vocal amplitude peaks the plateBlend value rises from 0.22 to a ceiling of 0.34 over 8 frames (spring-damped, k=0.18), then returns — the stone remembers the plate slightly more when the voice is present.
proposals.texture: Stone planes: a generated normal-map noise field (fractal Brownian motion, 4 octaves, lacunarity 2.1, gain 0.48) baked to a 1024×1024 offscreen canvas at init, never redrawn — it is geology, not animation. The primary seam and micro-fissures are rendered as emissive paths: strokeStyle #D4AF37, lineWidth varying from 2.4px (micro-fissures) to 6px (primary seam at its widest node), with a radial glow pass (shadow blur 28px, #D4AF37 at 60% alpha) drawn one frame before the stroke so the glow sits beneath the line, not on top of it. Lacquer repair nodes: circles of radius 8–14px at the three major branch-points of the primary seam, filled #FFF5D6 at 80% opacity, with a secondary glow (shadow blur 14px, #D4AF37). Film grain: a 512×512 noise canvas, redrawn each frame with Math.random() per pixel at alpha 0.04 — below the threshold of flicker perception at 60 fps, present as material memory. N
proposals.motion: Three envelopes, three responses, all properties of the existing geometry — nothing added, nothing repositioned. Vocal amplitude → luminance of the primary seam: the emissive glow radius breathes from shadow-blur 18px (silence) to 38px (peak vocal), spring-damped (k=0.14, damping=0.72), 60 fps. Swell amplitude → warm halation in the upper-right negative-space quadrant only: a radial gradient centered at the φ-intersection of the upper-right quadrant expands its outer radius from 12% to 28% of frame height, colour stop #D4AF37 at 0% opacity inner to 8% opacity outer — barely there, breathes with the swell, never competes with the seam. Harmonic content (spectral centroid, 800–4000 Hz band) → lacquer node opacity: the three repair nodes pulse from 70% to 100% opacity, each node phase-offset by 8 frames from its neighbour so they do not pulse in unison — they are a chord, not a flash. proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D render loop at 60 fps. Init sequence: (1) load and sample concept plate to 32×18 luminance map; (2) generate and cache stone normal-map noise to offscreen 1024×1024 canvas; (3) declare all fracture path coordinates as frozen constants (Object.freeze) before the first requestAnimationFrame call — the geometry is the constraint, not a runtime decision. Per-frame draw order: stone base gradient (#0E0E12 → #232229, radial, center-weighted to lower-left plane); multiply the cached normal-map at 0.15 opacity; multiply the concept plate at plateBlend (0.22–0.34); draw god-ray gradients terminating at luminance-map-authorized positions; draw glow passes for seam and nodes (shadow blur, drawn before strokes); draw seam and micro-fissure strokes; draw film grain overlay; draw text-safe scrim; draw lyric text. All generative, no external assets beyond the one concept plate.
proposals.humanTrace: The fracture path coordinates were derived by hand — a human decision about where the break falls, how far it deviates from the φ-line, where the three lacquer nodes sit. That editorial act is irreversible and non-algorithmic. The grain and the glow simulate material: paper-mineral surface, molten metal at 3500K. The stone remembers the plate's mineral record. The silence between lines is a directed choice, not a default.
proposals.risk: One seam is almost nothing. The Baroque Dramatist will call it inert. The risk is that restraint reads as poverty rather than precision — that congregations at forty metres see a dark screen with a gold line and feel abandoned rather than held. The risk is worth it because the alternative — a fracture network, multiple competing seams, branching animation — turns kintsugi's theology into spectacle. Kintsugi is about the one break that was healed. One seam is the argument. If the glow and the typography are precise, the emptiness of the upper-right quadrant becomes the most articulate thing in the room.
